sentence: Freeport-McMoRan's revenue rose by 60.9% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This increase was driven by higher sales volumes of copper and gold, with a 19 percent increase in copper sales volumes and a 59 percent increase in gold sales volumes compared to 2020 [3].

Additionally, higher realized prices for copper and molybdenum contributed to the revenue growth, with average realized prices 47 percent higher for copper and 53 percent higher for molybdenum compared to 2020 [7].
T-Mobile's revenue rose by 17.1% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This increase was primarily driven by higher average postpaid accounts and higher postpaid ARPA [3].
Booking Holdings' revenue rose by 61.2% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This increase was driven by the significant improvement in travel demand trends since the second quarter of 2020, which was severely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic [6].
Additionally, merchant revenues increased more year-over-year than agency revenues due to the expansion of merchant accommodation reservation services at Booking.com [6].
Monster Beverage's revenue rose by 20.5% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This growth was primarily driven by the $915.4 million increase in net sales for the Monster Energy® Drinks segment, which contributed to the overall revenue growth [8].
Phillips 66's revenue rose by 73.8% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This increase was mainly due to higher prices for refined petroleum products, crude oil, and NGL, as well as increased volumes for refined petroleum products and crude oil [7].
Goldman Sachs's revenue rose by 33.2% in fiscal 2021 [DB].

The increase was primarily driven by significantly higher compensation and benefits expenses reflecting strong performance, as well as higher technology expenses and professional fees, and higher transaction-based expenses [1].
These increases were partially offset by lower net provisions for litigation and regulatory proceedings and lower expenses related to consolidated investments [1].
Amgen's revenue rose by 18.6% in fiscal 2024 [DB].
This growth was primarily driven by volume growth of 23%, which was partially offset by declines in net selling price of 2% [2].
Additionally, product sales from acquired Horizon products contributed significantly, adding $4.2 billion in 2024 compared to $954 million in 2023 [2].
Caterpillar's revenue rose by 22.1% in fiscal 2021 [DB].

The increase was primarily due to higher sales volume, driven by higher end-user demand for equipment and services and the impact from changes in dealer inventories, along with favorable price realization [5].
Dealers decreased their inventories about $2.9 billion in 2020, compared to a decrease of about $100 million in 2021 [7].
Realty Income's revenue rose by 60.7% in fiscal 2022 [DB].
The increase in total revenue primarily relates to the merger with VEREIT and acquisitions for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021 [8].
Oracle's revenue rose by 17.7% in fiscal 2023 [DB].

This increase was primarily due to revenue contributions from the acquisition of Cerner, as well as growth in cloud services and license support revenues, increased demand for cloud license and on-premise license offerings, and growth in Oracle Exadata and other strategic hardware product offerings [1].
NextEra Energy's revenue rose by 22.8% in fiscal 2022 [DB].
The increase in revenue was primarily due to higher results at FPL and Corporate and Other, partly offset by lower results at NEER [5].
Newmont's revenue rose by 58.2% in fiscal 2024 [DB].

The increase in revenue was primarily due to higher average realized prices for all metals, lower Impairment charges, lower Reclamation and remediation costs, and higher net income at Peñasquito, which had been impacted in 2023 as a result of the labor strike [4].
Comcast's revenue rose by 12.4% in fiscal 2021 [DB].

The Sky segment also contributed to the growth through increased advertising and direct-to-consumer revenue, although this was partially offset by decreased content revenue and foreign currency translation effects [1][2].
Coca-Cola's revenue rose by 17.1% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This increase was primarily driven by a 9% growth in worldwide concentrate sales volume and an 8% increase in unit case volume compared to 2020 [4].

The growth was further supported by favorable pricing initiatives, favorable channel and category mix, effective cost management, and lower other operating charges, partially offset by higher annual incentive expense and increased marketing spending [6].
Additionally, the gradual recovery in away-from-home channels in many markets throughout 2021 contributed to the increase in unit case volume [2].
Marathon Petroleum's revenue rose by 71.9% in fiscal 2021 [DB].

This increase was primarily due to increased sales and other operating revenues of $50.20 billion, driven by increased average refined product sales prices of $0.80 per gallon, or 65 percent, and refined product sales volumes of 203 mbpd, or 6 percent, largely due to continuing economic recovery from the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 [6].
American Express' revenue rose by 17.4% in fiscal 2021 [DB].
This growth was driven by double-digit growth in all non-interest revenue lines, with discount revenue increasing 26% year-over-year, primarily due to growth in Card Member spending [3].
Other fees and commissions and other revenues also increased, mainly due to higher travel-related revenues [3].
Net card fees grew consistently throughout 2021, up 11% year-over-year, as new card acquisitions increased and Card Member retention remained high [3].
RTX's revenue rose by 17.1% in fiscal 2024 [DB].

Additionally, the organic operating profit increase of $0.6 billion in 2024 compared to 2023 reflects higher commercial aerospace operating profit and an increase in military operating profit of $0.2 billion, driven by the sales volume discussed and favorable sustainment mix [1][6].
Public Storage's revenue rose by 14.8% in fiscal 2022 [DB].
This increase is attributed to higher realized annual rent per occupied square foot, partially offset by a decline in occupancy [2].
Dominion Energy's revenue rose by 22.1% in fiscal 2022 [DB].
